cards.title: UI with intention
cards.body: I care about layout, hierarchy, spacing, and visual clarity. Good design should not only look good, it should make things easier to understand and use.

cards.title: Accessibility from the start
cards.body: I want interfaces to be readable, inclusive, and usable for more people. Accessibility is something I want to keep improving in every project.

cards.title: Component-based thinking
cards.body: I enjoy building reusable components and structured UI systems that make products easier to scale and maintain.

cards.title: Curious and fast-learning
cards.body: I learn quickly and enjoy exploring. It has led to me picking up things outside of courses and projects fairly often, and bringing them into the next thing I work on.

cards.title: People over process
cards.body: I believe the best results come from good communication and a positive atmosphere. I enjoy being part of a team, sharing ideas openly, and solving problems together with others, preferably over a cup of coffee or two.

about.title: About
about.body1: I'm a fullstack-trained developer with a strong interest in frontend, UI, accessibility, and user experience. I enjoy creating digital products that feel thoughtful, modern, and easy to use.
about.body2: My background includes school projects, internship work, client projects, and component-based frontend development. I've worked with UI implementation, Storybook, Figma, API integration, and both frontend and backend development.
about.body3: What drives me most is the combination of creativity and structure, finding ways to turn ideas, layouts, and user needs into real products. Outside of that, I'm a people person at heart. I genuinely enjoy collaborating, exchanging ideas, and being part of a team where everyone's working toward something together.
about.body4: Before moving into development, I completed a Bachelor's degree in Project Management, specialising in Media, Aesthetics and Cultural Entrepreneurship at the University of Gothenburg. That background shaped the way I think about communication, creative processes, and how to bring people and ideas together. It's something I carry into every project.

webdoc.intro: Webdoc Insights is an internal web application for visualising key metrics and building presentation views with dynamic content. The project consists of a dashboard, a presentation editor, and a presentation player.
webdoc.role1: I worked primarily with frontend development and UI, contributing to building reusable components in Storybook, developing widgets for statistics display, and creating various slides for presenting data such as weather, traffic, and key metrics.
webdoc.role2: The focus was on creating a flexible, modern, and clear user experience where data becomes more accessible and visually engaging.
webdoc.testimonialQuote2: Kasper has shown impressive technical skills in frontend development and delivered high-quality work. He is driven, attentive, and very skilled in his communication with both developers and other stakeholders. Kasper is also reliable and takes great responsibility for his tasks. As a person, he contributes warmth and positive energy that strengthens team spirit. I can warmly recommend Kasper for future projects.
webdoc.goal: Webdoc wanted a dashboard that gave a clear overview of their services, along with slides for Västtrafik departures, weather, and other dynamic content.
webdoc.challenge: One of the biggest challenges was connecting backend data to our widgets in a way that worked reliably and consistently. The data came from different sources and needed to be mapped correctly to each widget type, requiring precision and a clear understanding of both the data structures and the interface logic.
webdoc.solution: The key was communication. By keeping an ongoing dialogue with the backend team, we could identify early on what the data looked like, what needed to be adjusted, and where responsibilities lay. Many problems were solved faster by talking them through together rather than working in isolation, a clear reminder of how essential collaboration and clarity are in a shared system.
webdoc.outcome: The dashboard became more modular and easier to extend, with components reused consistently across multiple parts of the system. The project gave me a deeper understanding of how design systems, component thinking, and state management connect in larger interfaces, and how to build flexible UI solutions that still feel stable and well-considered for the user.

boomi.intro: A fast, social party game for 4–12 players. Players connect via mobile or desktop to a shared room where a pixelated bomb creature Boomi, is passed around during a 60-second round. One player secretly places Boomi. Everyone else tries to figure out who.
boomi.role1: Solo project, I handled everything from game design and UX to frontend development and deployment. This included building the real-time multiplayer flow with Firestore, designing the pixel UI system, implementing sprite animations with PixiJS, and adding sound effects and background music via Howler.js.
boomi.role2: The project was built over six weeks as part of a school exam, with a focus on playability, accessibility (WCAG 2.1 A/AA), and a coherent retro aesthetic throughout.
boomi.testimonialQuote: Kasper has demonstrated an impressive combination of technical skill, creativity and a strong drive for programming through his thesis. It is a project that truly stands out and clearly reflects both his high level of ambition and the great development he has made during his education, both in terms of skills and personally.
boomi.goal: The goal with Boomi Countdown was to challenge myself technically while improving my skills in UI/UX. I wanted to bring together what I had learned throughout my education and internship into a project that felt thorough, playful, and personal.
boomi.challenge: The hardest part was working with PixiJS. It required more logic than I initially expected, especially getting movements and animations to feel right. It was also a challenge to combine the technical side with a clear and fun user experience.
boomi.solution: I worked through it by testing and iterating a lot, and simplifying where needed. A key insight was that you don't always have to reinvent the wheel, some things turned out better and smoother to solve with something as straightforward as CSS transitions.
boomi.outcome: The end result was a project that reflected me as a developer, both technically and visually. I learned a lot about animation, logic, and the value of choosing smart solutions instead of doing everything the hard way. And above all, a playable game!

flinq.intro: Design and launch of a new website for Flinq, a company focused on cost savings and analysis within supply chain. The goal was to quickly communicate business value, build trust, and make it easy for potential customers to take the next step.
flinq.about1: The project involved designing and launching a website that clearly explained what Flinq does, what problem they solve, and how to get in touch, with business value and user experience at the centre.
flinq.about2: The site was built using One, which enabled an efficient workflow where design, content, and structure could be developed in parallel. This allowed for quick iteration and landing on a solution that is easy to maintain and ready to scale.
flinq.goal: The goal with the Flinq project was to create a website that clearly communicates what the company offers and why it's valuable to the customer. I wanted to build something that felt professional, trustworthy, and easy to take in, with a focus on structure, speed, and clear communication.
flinq.challenge: The biggest challenge was working within One's website builder, which had limitations in both responsiveness and how freely you could work with components. That pushed me to think more creatively to make the site feel modern and polished despite the tool's constraints.
flinq.solution: I solved it by focusing on what actually made the biggest difference: clear structure, solid content, and a simple but considered design. Instead of getting stuck on the tool's limitations, I tried to use them smartly and adapt the layout so the site worked as well as possible across screen sizes.
flinq.outcome: The end result was a website the client was happy with and that served its purpose clearly. What I took away from the project was above all that a good result isn't always about having full technical freedom, it's about being adaptable, prioritising well, and creating value within the constraints you're given.

akarui.intro: A full-stack e-commerce web application for a fictional candle brand. Built as a group assignment covering a complete webshop with product listings, cart, checkout, order confirmation, and an admin panel for managing products.
akarui.goal: The goal was to apply what we had learned in a realistic, full-stack setting, working as a group on a shared codebase while using technologies like Next.js App Router and Server Actions that were new to us. We wanted the end result to feel like a real product, not just a school assignment.
akarui.challenge: One of the biggest challenges was coordinating the work across the group while keeping the code consistent. We were also working with Next.js App Router and Server Actions for the first time, which meant understanding a new mental model for how data flows between client and server.
akarui.solution: We divided responsibilities clearly early on and kept communication ongoing throughout the project. Using Server Actions for all CRUD operations gave us a clean and consistent pattern across the whole app, and Prisma made the database layer straightforward to work with once we had the schema in place.
akarui.outcome: The biggest takeaway was how much smoother a group project runs when structure and communication are prioritised from the start. I also got a solid understanding of how Server Actions and Prisma work together in a real app, and how much a consistent pattern across the codebase reduces friction when multiple people are working on the same thing. On top of that, I created all product images and mockups for the store, and implemented dark mode, which taught me a lot about theming, CSS variables, and thinking in design systems.
